rationale:
`requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.ValidationContext.node_id` has one obligation: return a borrowed `&NodeId<D>` that identifies the source node the context was created for.

`crates/trust-but-verify/src/graph/validation_tests.rs#fn[labeled_selections_track_only_target_membership_without_reading_contents]` is marked `{test}` for it. The test builds `ValidationContext::new(&graph, intern_node(1))` and asserts `ctx.node_id() == &intern_node(1)`. That checks that the accessor returns the identity the context was constructed with. The borrow is enforced by the signature `&self -> &NodeId<D>`, so no runtime test is needed for it.

The test uses only one node. The accessor has no conditional or transformation of its own. It only exposes the stored identity, so a second input class would not add a required distinction.

Other tests also call `ctx.node_id()`. `Memory::run_review` uses it to look up node data. Several `execute` implementations use it to read the node's contents. They are not marked as tests for this requirement, and I did not rely on them.

`crates/trust-but-verify/tests/public_api.rs#fn[public_exports_match_the_appendix]` covers the public signature through the export inventory. I found no gap.

text: Borrow the identity of the source node being checked.
